Fixed range reviewed: `aa1ea64e7c3f431c8b0c2cb2385d6e6b6d5c304d...38cf3a1680b345b5f177f4978b1afc3700efa122`. Both commits resolve, the merge-base is the supplied base, and the diff is non-empty (3 commits, 7 files). One canonical sibling-parallel Standards/Spec batch was used. No archived session payloads were inspected; no scratch/probe changes were made.

## Standards

1. **High — Cleanup ordering contradicts frozen promotion law and makes Recorder outcome recording impossible.** Prior accepted authority requires promotion “only after … required raw cleanup” and treats cleanup failure as Recorder failure (`.ak/dockets/issues/10/authority/judge-001/receipt.json:4`). Amendments instead delete scratch “only after … hot finalization” and “after successful core promotion” (`.ak/dockets/issues/10/authority/amendments/004-hot-claim-chain-and-cold-forensic-stream.md:29`; `.ak/dockets/issues/10/authority/amendments/005-value-bearing-evidence-only.md:13`). Because the manifest must contain the Recorder outcome (`.ak/dockets/issues/10/authority/amendments/003-evidence-admission-and-core-docket.md:13`), a post-promotion cleanup failure leaves an apparently complete manifest with a stale success outcome. Amendment 005 explicitly supersedes only automatic cold retention, not the frozen cleanup invariant (`.ak/dockets/issues/10/authority/amendments/005-value-bearing-evidence-only.md:3`).

2. **High — Admitted ranges have no exact-byte identity.** Amendment 005 says a cited “object/range” enters the claim chain (`.ak/dockets/issues/10/authority/amendments/005-value-bearing-evidence-only.md:24`), while amendment 004 seals only whole-stream/object lengths and digests (`.ak/dockets/issues/10/authority/amendments/004-hot-claim-chain-and-cold-forensic-stream.md:9`). No coordinate basis, framing, reconstructed offsets, or range digest is defined. Such an exhibit cannot satisfy exact-byte preservation (`docs/development-closure.md:50-54`). **Mysterious Name** (judgment call): the quoted hunk “the specifically cited object/range” leaves “range” semantically unknowable.

3. **Medium — Raw regression retention bypasses probe lifecycle.** “Owner-approved behavioral recording or regression exhibit” is retained in external cold storage (`.ak/dockets/issues/10/authority/amendments/005-value-bearing-evidence-only.md:17,24`) without requiring graduation exactly once into the affected seam’s regression suite and deletion of scratch. That conflicts with the probe-lifecycle rule in `CLAUDE.md:39-41`: after a probe’s evidence purpose is disposed, it must be deleted or graduated exactly once, with no duplicate permanent shape.

4. **Medium — The cold-store interface is expressly hypothetical and shallow.** V1 introduces a “cold-root filesystem seam” while admitting only a future second adapter could justify a broader interface (`.ak/dockets/issues/10/authority/amendments/004-hot-claim-chain-and-cold-forensic-stream.md:31-33`). This breaches “one adapter means a hypothetical seam” (`/Users/akagilnc/.agents/skills/codebase-design/SKILL.md:65`) and offloads durability, permissions, retention, and availability to callers, reducing locality as defined by the deep-module standard (`/Users/akagilnc/.agents/skills/codebase-design/SKILL.md:28`). **Speculative Generality** (judgment call): “A future second real adapter may justify…” is the quoted speculative seam.

## Spec

### (a) Requirements missing or partial

1. **Forward Git sealing has no required terminal transition or owner.** Governing law requires “freeze a non-circular forward sealing lifecycle” (`.ak/dockets/issues/10/authority/judge-004/receipt.json:4`), and the normal boundary requires “sealed authority/task identity” (`.ak/dockets/issues/10/authority/amendments/005-value-bearing-evidence-only.md:7`). Yet sealing merely “may” occur later, with no deadline or failure state, allowing artifacts to remain pending indefinitely (`.ak/dockets/issues/10/authority/amendments/004-hot-claim-chain-and-cold-forensic-stream.md:21`).

2. **Cold-before-hot failure leaves an unspecified durable-object state.** Judge-004 requires admission/reconstruction failures to obey cleanup and atomic-promotion law (`.ak/dockets/issues/10/authority/judge-004/receipt.json:4`). The contract writes and verifies cold storage before hot promotion, but on hot-promotion failure specifies only infrastructure precedence and scratch cleanup—not whether the cold object and locator are retained, removed, or recoverably reported (`.ak/dockets/issues/10/authority/amendments/004-hot-claim-chain-and-cold-forensic-stream.md:25,29,33`).

3. **Branch reconstruction does not require exact preservation of superseded manifests.** Governing law says accepted artifacts retain exact bytes and replacements preserve the prior artifact through forward disposition (`docs/development-closure.md:50-53`). Requiring “manifests corrected for omitted payloads” without requiring the original manifests plus append-only replacements permits loss of canonical claim-chain evidence during reconstruction (`.ak/dockets/issues/10/authority/amendments/005-value-bearing-evidence-only.md:28`).

### (b) Unasked scope creep

None found.

### (c) Apparently implemented requirements whose contract is wrong

4. **Cold streams violate Git-reference-only law.** The governing direction requires reference-only treatment “for every byte already exactly recoverable” (`.ak/dockets/issues/10/authority/request-004.md:5`). Amendment 004 instead deliberately recopies embedded Git bytes into cold streams as an “explicit cold-stream exception” (`.ak/dockets/issues/10/authority/amendments/004-hot-claim-chain-and-cold-forensic-stream.md:17`).

5. **Failure retention is neither irreducibility-bounded nor always workable.** The governing rule is “preserve what carries a claim, decision, or irreducible proof” (`.ak/dockets/issues/10/authority/amendments/005-value-bearing-evidence-only.md:30`), but any predeclared child/Recorder failure class authorizes retention without evidentiary necessity (`.ak/dockets/issues/10/authority/amendments/005-value-bearing-evidence-only.md:19`). This also includes redaction, scanning, or cold-write failures recognized at `.ak/dockets/issues/10/authority/amendments/004-hot-claim-chain-and-cold-forensic-stream.md:29`—classes where credential-safe cold retention may be impossible.

**Summary:** Standards: 4 findings; worst is the cleanup/promotion-order contradiction. Spec: 5 findings; worst is the admitted cold-stream exception to Git-reference-only storage.
